messages:
customer_jenny: Hey team — running into a weird one with /v1/rerank/batch. We send 3 queries with per-query candidate lists but the scores look shifted by one candidate for queries 2 and 3. No errors in response (200) but top results are wrong.

maria_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you share a minimal reproducer and the exact request body?

customer_jenny: Pasting a trimmed version of the payload we use (we upload as CSV converted to JSONL on our side):
```json
{
  "queries": [
    {"id": "q1", "text": "find widget"},
    {"id": "q2", "text": "install guide"},
    {"id": "q3", "text": "troubleshoot leak"}
  ],
  "candidates_per_query": [
    ["c1","c2","c3"],
    ["d1","d2","d3","d4"],
    ["e1","e2"]
  ]
}
```
response body returns scores array flat-encoded and the pairing seems off. We only see it when candidates counts vary.

ingrid_eng: Can you paste the response (redact PII)? Is the returned array length equal to sum(candidates)?

customer_jenny: Yep length matches. Example returned scores (flat): [0.9,0.2,0.1, 0.3,0.4,0.6,0.1, 0.5,0.4] — for q2 it returned 4 scores but they appear mapped to q2 candidates out of order.

sean_oncall: Any chance of CSV -> JSONL converter adding an empty string candidate or stray separator? We've seen CRLF + trailing comma cause an empty token that shifts offsets.

customer_jenny: Interesting — we do generate CSV first, then convert. Our CSV rows look like: id,query,candidates
q1,find widget,"c1|||c2|||c3"
q2,install guide,"d1|||d2|||d3|||d4"
q3,troubleshoot leak,"e1|||e2"

maria_support: Ah — you're using a custom delimiter `|||`. The converter splits on `|` first for some libs if not escaped properly. Can you run a quick check: print counts after split on your end before calling the API?

customer_jenny: Confirmed — in one production run the split yielded an extra empty string for q2: ["d1","d2","","d3","d4"]. That would explain the shift.

ingrid_eng: Good catch. Two follow-ups: 1) we'll add server-side validation to detect empty candidate tokens and return 400 with a helpful message, 2) we'll update docs to warn about multi-char separators and trimming.

sean_oncall: For immediate workaround, ensure trimming and filter empty strings in your conversion step. Example JS snippet: `candidates = raw.split('|||').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean)`

customer_jenny: That fixed the mapping in our staging tests. Thanks. One more thing — during the bad runs our billing spikes because we re-ran retries — is there a way to get a credit or flag those requests? The requests themselves returned 200 so they counted.

maria_support: Sorry about the billing noise — open a support ticket with the request IDs and timestamps and we'll escalate for a review. If you can include the original and corrected payloads that's helpful.

support-bot: Incident note created: INC-2024-455 — assigned to billing.

ingrid_eng: Long-term fix: we'll add stricter schema validation for nested candidate lists and a warning on CSV import. Also adding a quick debug header `X-Rerank-Candidate-Checksum` so clients can detect mismatch between declared counts and payload.

customer_jenny: Appreciate it. Also saw occasional latency spikes when we retried many small multiquery batches — any tuning tips?

sean_oncall: If you have many short queries, try batching at the client into a single /batch call with explicit per-query candidate offsets. We also have autoscaling bursts but small high-concurrency spikes can add queueing delays. Share a sample QPS and we can advise.

customer_jenny: QPS ~120 bursts to 400 for <1m. We'll work on smoothing and will send ticket for billing/IDs. Thanks all :white_check_mark:

maria_support: Thanks for the detailed repro and for confirming the workaround. We'll keep this thread updated when ENG rolls the validation and doc updates. :thumbsup:
